---
title: "Getting Financial Data - quantmod - Solutions"
output: html_document
---

### Introduction:

This time you will get data from a website.
The original exercise uses pandas-datareader with an AlphaVantage API key.
In R we use the `quantmod` package, which downloads the data from Yahoo Finance
without needing an API key.

### Step 1. Import the necessary libraries

```{r step1, message=FALSE}
# package to download financial data into R
# make sure you have it installed: install.packages("quantmod")
library(quantmod)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(tibble)
library(lubridate)
```

### Step 2. Create your time range (start and end variables). The start date should be 01/01/2015 and the end should today (whatever your today is).

```{r}
start <- as.Date("2015-01-01")
end <- Sys.Date()

start
```

### Step 3. Make sure that quantmod is installed and loaded.

Yahoo Finance does not require an API key. (If you prefer AlphaVantage, quantmod also supports it with
`getSymbols(..., src = "av", api.key = "your_key")`.)

### Step 4. Use quantmod to read the daily time series for the Apple stock (ticker symbol AAPL) between 01/01/2015 and today, assign it to df_apple and print it.

```{r}
# getSymbols() returns an xts object (a time series indexed by date).
# This helper turns it into a tibble with a date column and simple column names.
get_stock <- function(ticker) {
  x <- getSymbols(ticker, src = "yahoo", from = start, to = end, auto.assign = FALSE)
  df <- as_tibble(as.data.frame(x))
  names(df) <- tolower(sub(".*\\.", "", names(df))) # "AAPL.Open" -> "open"
  df |> mutate(date = as.Date(index(x)), .before = 1)
}

df_apple <- get_stock("AAPL")

df_apple
```

### Step 5. Add a new column "stock" to the dataframe and add the ticker symbol

```{r}
df_apple <- df_apple |> mutate(stock = "AAPL")
df_apple
```

### Step 6. Repeat the two previous steps for a few other stocks, always creating a new dataframe: Tesla, IBM and Microsoft. (Ticker symbols TSLA, IBM and MSFT.)

```{r}
# Tesla
df_tesla <- get_stock("TSLA") |> mutate(stock = "TSLA")

# IBM
df_ibm <- get_stock("IBM") |> mutate(stock = "IBM")

# Microsoft
df_microsoft <- get_stock("MSFT") |> mutate(stock = "MSFT")
```

### Step 7. Combine the four separate dataFrames into one combined dataFrame df that holds the information for all four stocks

```{r}
df <- bind_rows(df_apple, df_tesla, df_ibm, df_microsoft)
df
```

### Step 8. Shift the stock column into the index (making it a multi-level index consisting of the ticker symbol and the date).

```{r}
# R has no multi-level index. The equivalent is to put the key columns first
# and sort by them (or to use group_by(stock) for later calculations).
df <- df |>
  relocate(stock, date) |>
  arrange(stock, date)
df
```

### Step 9. Create a dataFrame called vol, with the volume values.

```{r}
vol <- df |> select(stock, date, volume)
vol
```

### Step 10. Aggregate the data of volume to weekly.

Hint: Be careful to not sum data from the same week of 2015 and other years.

```{r}
# isoyear() and isoweek() give the ISO year and week number of each date,
# so the same week number of different years stays separate
vol <- vol |> mutate(year = isoyear(date), week = isoweek(date))

vol |>
  group_by(year, week, stock) |>
  summarise(volume = sum(volume), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stock, values_from = volume)
```

### Step 11. Find all the volume traded in the year of 2015

```{r}
vol |>
  filter(year(date) == 2015) |>
  group_by(stock) |>
  summarise(volume = sum(volume)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = stock, values_from = volume)
```
